title: cross-review findings
description: Per-reviewer output contract. Each reviewer numbers its own findings with a reviewer prefix (GLM => 'G-001', Claude => 'C-001'). The synthesizer (Claude) reassigns canonical 'F-###' ids when merging.

summary.description: 2-3 sentence overall read. Per the discipline prompt, findings come first; this is for the human, not a lead-in for the reviewer.

passes_total.description: Multi-pass only: how many reviewer-#2 passes produced valid output and were aggregated. The honest denominator for pass_count. Absent on single-pass output.

id.description: Reviewer-prefixed id, e.g. 'G-001' (GLM) or 'C-001' (Claude). Stable within this review.

location.description: file:line for diffs, or section name for designs.

issue.description: What is wrong (one or two sentences).

evidence.description: Concrete grounding: the diff line / spec clause / observed behavior that proves the issue. Reduces hallucinated findings.

failure_case.description: A concrete scenario where this bites (input, sequence, or load that triggers it).

recommendation.description: This reviewer's recommended CALL on its own finding. Distinct from the synthesizer's canonical disposition: a reviewer recommends, the chair decides. There is deliberately no 'reject' value, since a blind reviewer never rejects a finding it just raised; only the synthesizer rejects. Severity is impact, recommendation is action, and they may diverge (a low-severity item with a one-line fix can be must_fix; a high-severity item outside this change's scope can be defer). Required so that 'the two reviewers' recommendation values differ' is derivable from reviewer output rather than guessed.

pass_count.description: Multi-pass only: how many reviewer-#2 passes raised this finding (out of passes_total). Written by aggregate_passes.py, never by a single pass. A ranking/confidence signal, never a filter: a pass_count of 1 is still a real finding.

speculative.description: true if this is a plausible-but-unverified concern. Optional; defaults false.

allOf.//: Evidence + failure_case are mandatory for the findings most worth grounding.
Correctness/security claims must be grounded regardless of severity.
